categories.main_business_segments: As of August 31, 2024, Jabil operated two main segments: Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) and Diversified Manufacturing Services (DMS). EMS focuses on high-volume, core electronics manufacturing for industries such as 5G, wireless, cloud, industrial, and networking. DMS emphasizes engineering solutions, material sciences, and healthcare, serving automotive, connected devices, and packaging industries. Beginning September 1, 2024, Jabil will reorganize into three segments: Regulated Industries, Intelligent Infrastructure, and Connected Living and Digital Commerce.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Jabil leverages highly automated, continuous flow manufacturing, advanced electronic and mechanical design, and global supply chain management. Core technologies include automation, advanced polymer and metal material science, injection molding, additive manufacturing, digital printing, co-packaged optics, silicon photonics, and AI/machine learning. The company employs a decentralized business unit model, computerized control systems, and electronic supply chain management tools.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Jabil serves leading companies across diverse industries, including cloud and data infrastructure, healthcare, automotive and transportation, packaging, warehouse automation, networking, and semi-capital equipment. Its customer base is concentrated, with the five largest customers accounting for 36% of net revenue in 2024; Apple, Inc. represented 11%. The company targets customers seeking highly automated, global manufacturing solutions.
categories.geographic_coverage: Jabil operates in more than 30 countries, with major manufacturing sites in China, Mexico, Singapore, Malaysia, and the United States. In 2024, 82.5% of net revenue was generated from foreign sources. The company maintains approximately 100 locations worldwide, with a significant presence in Asia, the Americas, and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Jabil operates as a contract manufacturer and supply chain solutions provider, primarily in the downstream portion of the supply chain. It is responsible for design, procurement, assembly, testing, and delivery of finished products built to customer specifications, often managing end-to-end product and component flows.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Jabil's strategy emphasizes long-term customer relationships, product and customer diversification, customer-centric business units, and leveraging its global production footprint. R&D focuses on advanced manufacturing processes, automation, sustainable materials, AI/ML, and new product introduction capabilities. The company selectively pursues acquisitions to expand capabilities and enter new markets.
categories.revenue_model: Jabil generates revenue primarily through turnkey manufacturing services, which include product design, production, and product management. Revenue is recognized over time as products are manufactured to customer specifications, with additional income from design services and supply chain management. The company also offers configure-to-order and direct-order fulfillment services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Jabil competes with global EMS providers such as Flex Ltd., Celestica Inc., Hon Hai Precision (Foxconn), Plexus Corp., and Sanmina Corp., as well as with customers' internal manufacturing operations. The company is positioned as a leading, technologically advanced, and trusted manufacturing solutions provider, emphasizing global scale, advanced technology, and customer-centricity.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended August 31, 2024, Jabil reported net revenue of $28.9 billion and net income of $1.4 billion. The company experienced a 16.8% revenue decline from 2023, primarily due to the divestiture of its Mobility Business and changes in customer demand. Jabil maintains strong liquidity, significant global assets, and a history of consistent profitability.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Jabil differentiates itself through its global manufacturing scale, advanced automation, engineering and design capabilities, and customer-centric business unit model. The company offers accelerated time-to-market, efficient supply chain management, access to advanced technologies, and the ability to deliver high-quality, customized solutions across diverse industries and geographies.
